Log-likelihood contributions per observation or per group

Source: R/loglik-contrib.R
brs_loglik_contrib.Rd

The terms whose sum is the log-likelihood: one per observation for a brs fit, and one per group (cluster) for a brsmm fit, the marginal log-likelihood of the group's observations with its random effects integrated out. With newdata, the contributions of new observations at the fitted parameters (held-out scoring).

Usage

brs_loglik_contrib(object, newdata = NULL, int_method = NULL, n_points = NULL)

Arguments

object

A fitted "brs" or "brsmm" object.

newdata

Optional data frame of new observations (see Details).

int_method, n_points

For brsmm fits: integration rule ("laplace", "aghq" or "qmc") and number of nodes (nodes per dimension for "aghq", points for "qmc"); NULL (default) uses those of the fit. Ignored for brs fits.

Value

Named numeric vector: by row name of the data (brs) or by group level (brsmm, with attribute "n", the number of observations of each group).

Details

For a brs fit the contribution of a score row is \(\log P(S = s_i)\), the log probability of its cell (the log density for exact observations, \(\delta = 0\)), computed as in the compiled likelihood. For a brsmm fit the contribution of group \(g\) is $$\log \int \prod_i P(S = s_{gi} \mid b)\, \varphi(b; 0, D)\, db,$$ computed by the fit's int_method and n_points (or qmc_points) unless int_method / n_points are given. With the defaults and newdata = NULL, the contributions add up to logLik(object) (under "laplace", up to the tolerance of the inner mode search, about \(10^{-8}\)). A group without a positive-definite random-effect mode, which adds a penalty value to the fitted log-likelihood, gets NA with a warning.

With newdata, rows need the response, the covariates and (for brsmm) the grouping variable; rows with missing values in them are dropped. The groups need not be groups of the fit: their random effects are integrated out, so no random-effect estimate is used. Scores are coarsened with the cells of the fit (its estimated cutpoints under cutpoints = "boundary"). For score data the contributions are log probabilities of the observed scores (no Jacobian term), on the same scale as the log-likelihood of any model that gives a probability mass function on \(0, \ldots, K\).

See also

logLik.brsmm, brsmm_cv, brs_marginal

Examples

set.seed(21)
nrs <- expand.grid(id = 1:30, time = c("6h", "12h", "24h"))
b0 <- rnorm(30, sd = 0.8)
eta <- -1.3 + c(0, 0.75, 0.3)[nrs$time] + b0[nrs$id]
shp <- brs_repar(mu = plogis(eta), phi = 0.2, repar = 2)
nrs$y <- round(10 * rbeta(nrow(nrs), shp$shape1, shp$shape2))
m <- brsmm(y ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, data = nrs, ncuts = 10)

ll_g <- brs_loglik_contrib(m)
head(ll_g)
#>         1         2         3         4         5         6 
#> -6.019919 -6.321018 -7.271889 -5.779475 -8.037281 -8.350358 
c(sum = sum(ll_g), logLik = as.numeric(logLik(m)))
#>       sum    logLik 
#> -192.9768 -192.9768 
# Same groups, adaptive Gauss-Hermite with 31 nodes
head(brs_loglik_contrib(m, int_method = "aghq", n_points = 31))
#>         1         2         3         4         5         6 
#> -6.002478 -6.304053 -7.253131 -5.763656 -8.019587 -8.333486
